title: Quantum-enhanced sensing in a driven-dissipative system via chiral waveguide
authors: Yan Xi Foo, Saubhik Sarkar, Leong Chuan Kwek, Abolfazl Bayat, Davit Aghamalyan
abstract: Quantum sensors can achieve precision unattainable by classical sensors. However, dissipation coming from interaction with the environment can greatly degrade the performance of quantum sensors. Therefore, it is crucial to attempt harnessing dissipation to our advantage and investigate the sensing performance of driven-dissipative systems to gain practical quantum advantages. In this paper, we study a system of two-level systems driven coherently at a detuned frequency, and importantly, connected to a chiral waveguide that serves both as an interaction mediator and a bath. We show analytically that the steady state of such a system shows enhanced sensitivity to estimate weak detuning strength while the probe preparation time only grows linearly with system size. Therefore, the enhanced sensitivity is sustained even when the preparation time is incorporated. We further establish measurement protocols to achieve such sensitivity that are experimentally implementable. The chirality of the waveguide helps us to control both precision and range of enhanced sensitivity.
summary: This paper investigates quantum sensing in a realistic, open quantum system modeled by emitters coupled to a chiral waveguide. It shows that the steady state achieved through dissipation can yield enhanced sensitivity to weak detuning. Crucially, the authors prove that this enhanced sensitivity scales favorably with system size even when the necessary preparation time is accounted for.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of achieving quantum-enhanced sensing precision in physical systems where environmental dissipation is present.
main_result: It analytically demonstrates that the steady state of a driven-dissipative system coupled to a chiral waveguide exhibits enhanced sensitivity to weak detuning, and this advantage is maintained even when considering the finite preparation time.
method: The analysis involves solving the Lindblad master equation to find the steady state and calculating the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) to quantify sensing limits.
model_or_system: The system consists of $N$ two-level emitters arranged in a 1D array, coherently driven, and coupled to a chiral waveguide that acts as both an interaction mediator and a bath.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information ($F_E$), Classical Fisher Information (CFI), and the preparation time ($T$).
important_parameters: The degree of chirality ($\eta$), the system size ($N$), and the detuning strength ($\delta_j$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the Markovian regime and utilizes the steady state of the master equation as the sensing probe.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup (emitter array coupled to a chiral waveguide), the scaling of QFI/CFI with detuning strength, and the linear scaling of the preparation time $T$ with system size $N$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the physical model (driven-dissipative system) to deriving the scaling laws for sensing enhancement using the steady state, and finally confirming the feasibility by analyzing the linear scaling of the required preparation time.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the crucial issue of harnessing engineered dissipation (a core topic in open quantum systems) to maintain or enhance quantum advantages in sensing protocols, moving beyond idealized closed-system models.
